newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor takes control of casino firm SPIC.
newsitem.headline: Accor takes control of casino firm SPIC.

text.p: Hotel group Accor said on Monday that it had acquired control of France's fourth-largest casino company SPIC after buying stakes in the firm from media company Pathe and Sun International.
Accor, a co-founder of SPIC (Societe de Participations et d'Investissements de Casinos), said it held 65 percent after purchasing 25 percent from Sun and 15 percent from Pathe.
SPIC owns casinos in Nice, Cassis, Carry le Rouet and Chamonix and was recently given the casino concession for the spa town of Dax known for its thermal baths.
Accor did not disclose the terms of the deal, but said in a statement that SPIC's annual turnover was 550 million francs.
Accor also holds 34.9 percent of the firm SHCD, which operates casinos in Deauville, Trouville, Enghien, Ouistreham and Menton.
"By taking control of SPIC, Accor plans to be a major player in casinos in France," the company said. It said the casino business nicely complemented its core hotel business.
